text:
maria: Heads-up — eu-west1c is ejecting a lot of tiny GPU pods right now (~120 in 30m). Pattern looks like AZ-local binpacking is leaving 1-2 GPUs half-full and tiny-gang pods get evicted when a large pod lands. cc @tomas @ajay :eyes:

ajay: Yep, I saw a NIC/egress spike on those racks at the same time. Suspect inter-node NVLink vs host NIC contention -> kubelet preempting to recover. Not just storage evicts.

tomas: Can you paste a short scheduler/kubelet event snippet? Also what node taints/affinity rules are these tiny-gang pods using?

maria: Paste from one affected job: 
```
Events:
  Normal   Scheduled   5m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/job-tiny-abc to gpu-node-12
  Warning  Evicted     4m   kubelet            The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage.
  Normal   Killing     4m   kubelet            Stopping container
  Warning  Preempted   4m   default-scheduler  Preempting for higher priority pod
```
The pods have nodeAffinity preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: prefer same-az and they use tolerations for gpu:shared.

lenka: If scheduler strictly prefers AZ-local packing we get fragmentation (full racks + half-used GPUs). We can either: 1) relax AZ affinity for tiny-gang (spread across AZs) or 2) improve co-packing heuristics to favor filling partial GPUs first. Option 1 increases cross-AZ egress/cost and slightly higher tail latency.

chris: Quick experiment idea: enable `allow-az-spread` for only tiny-gang label via a rollout flag. That should reduce localized fragmentation. We should run a dry-run in staging to estimate egress delta.

ajay: Agreed on a targeted flag. Also want to try a scheduler predicate tweak: prefer nodes with >20% free GPU on same rack before rescheduling across AZ. Might reduce NIC spikes.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: feat/scheduler-az-spread-toggle -> canary to eu-west1-staging at 2026-03-21T02:00Z

maria: Action list: 
- @tomas: run a staging dry-run with allow-az-spread=true for label tiny-gang and capture egress + eviction rates (task: SRV-2432)
- @ajay: monitor NIC/egress on the two affected racks during the canary window
- @lenka: prepare a cost estimate (cross-AZ egress) and rollback criteria

chris: I'll draft the scheduler config patch (small change in topology scoring) and include a perf test in the canary. If staging looks good we can roll to eu-west1 in the next maintenance window.

maria: Thanks — will open a short incident ticket and schedule the 02:00 UTC canary. If we still see >50 evicts/hour after the flag, we'll rollback and iterate. :thumbsup:
